response.content:
## Companies That Expanded to Germany in 2026

Based on available reporting, several notable companies expanded into or significantly deepened their presence in Germany during 2026:

### New Market Entries

- **Waymo** (Alphabet subsidiary, USA) — Registered a German entity called **Waymo Germany GmbH** in June 2026 to prepare for autonomous ride-hailing services in Germany, marking its first move into the European market.

- **WB GROUP** (Poland) — Poland's largest privately owned defence company officially launched **WB GERMANY** in Berlin on November 10, 2026, and inaugurated its first German technology company based in Bavaria, strengthening German-Polish defence-industrial cooperation.

- **Pudu Robotics** (China) — Opened its **European headquarters in Neuss, Germany** in October 2026, consolidating sales, training, warehousing, and after-sales services to support its growing robotics business across Europe.

- **Longpoint Partners** (USA) — Announced in June 2026 its expansion into Germany (and the Netherlands), establishing a presence in Düsseldorf and Frankfurt with plans to deploy approximately **€400 million** into infill logistics assets.

- **Telekom Srbija** (Serbia) — Opened its **9th retail shop** in Germany (Offenbach) in March 2026, continuing to build a nationwide retail and distribution network in one of Europe's largest telecom markets.

- **Beks Media** — Opened a new office in **Berlin** as a central hub for its European operations.

- **Xunce** (China) — Expanded its AI data infrastructure product **TokenOS** into Germany, launching a "scenario Token factory" for the European market.

### Major Investment Expansions by Existing Players

- **Amazon** (USA) — Announced plans to invest over **€16 billion** in Germany in 2027, covering cloud/AI (AWS Frankfurt), logistics, satellite internet, and Prime Video, building on more than €100 billion invested since 2010.

- **NTT DATA** (Japan) — Advanced its **Frankfurt 6 data center campus** in Nierstein (January 2026) and won a contract for a **36 MW data center in Berlin** (July 2026).

- **Siemens** (Germany) — Announced a **€300 million** German investment in electrical distribution equipment manufacturing in July 2026.

- **Schwarz Group** (Germany) — Advanced a large **240 MW data center** development near Rostock in August 2026.

- **Crédit Agricole** (France) — Reported to be plotting expansion in Germany as a "priority market" following an acquisition relaunch in November 2026.

- **Deutsche Telekom** (Germany) — Invested nearly **€250 million** to expand its Munich AI Factory (launched February 2026), doubling capacity to 20 MW with Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs, serving industrial clients including Siemens and Daimler Truck.

# ► WB GROUP expands into Germany

Jules Roukoz [...] # ► WB GROUP expands into Germany

Jules Roukoz

WB GROUP, Poland’s largest privately owned defence company, is expanding into Germany. On 10 November, the Group officially launched WB GERMANY in Berlin and inaugurated its first German technology company, based in Bavaria, marking a further step towards closer German-Polish industrial and defence cooperation.

The event in the German capital was hosted by Piotr Wojciechowski, founder and President of WB GROUP. The Polish defence group sees Germany as a strategic market and an important partner in building a strong and technologically sovereign European defence industry capable of strengthening security on NATO’s eastern flank.

context.content: # Pudu Robotics Opens European Headquarters in Germany to Support Continued Growth Across the Region. NEUSS, Germany, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pudu Robotics, a global leader in commercial robotics, today announced the opening of its European headquarters in Neuss, Germany, strengthening its local operating capabilities as its business continues to expand across the region. The new headquarters brings together **sales, product demonstrations, training, warehousing and after-sales services**, reinforcing Pudu Robotics' investment in the local infrastructure and customer support needed to scale robotic deployments across European markets. Pudu Robotics Opens European Headquarters in Germany. The company continues to invest in local capabilities to strengthen collaboration with customers and partners and provide support throughout the deployment lifecycle. Looking ahead, Pudu Robotics will continue to develop its local operating capabilities, deepen collaboration with regional partners and expand the application of its robotic solutions across industries, supporting customers as robotics becomes increasingly integrated into everyday operations.

document.name: Pudu Robotics Opens European Headquarters in Germany to Support Continued Growth Across the Region

context.content: # Longpoint Expands into Germany and the Netherlands, Targeting €400 Million of Infill Logistics Investment. **BOSTON, June 09, 2026**--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Longpoint Partners today announced its expansion into Germany and the Netherlands, extending its infill industrial strategy into two of Europe's most supply-constrained logistics markets. The firm is establishing a presence in high-demand locations, including Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, and the Randstad, and plans to deploy approximately €400 million into logistics assets near major population centers and transportation corridors. "We are excited to expand Longpoint's infill industrial strategy into Germany and the Netherlands," said Dwight Angelini, Founding and Managing Partner of Longpoint Partners. Gijs Vissers joins as Netherlands Country Head, bringing more than 16 years of experience in Dutch real estate and involvement in more than €4 billion of transactions. Earlier, he spent seven years at Palmira Capital Partners, where he helped grow the firm from €260 million to more than €2.0 billion in assets under management and participated in 57 acquisitions totaling €1.2 billion.

document.name: Longpoint Expands into Germany and the Netherlands, Targeting €400 Million of Infill Logistics Investment

context.content: # Telekom Srbija to Open 9th Shop in Germany, Marking Expansion Milestone. *Opening of 9th retail store in Offenbach on March 26 highlights Germany as a key growth market*. **BELGRADE, Serbia, March 20, 2026**--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Telekom Srbija Group will open its 9th retail shop in Germany on March 26 in Offenbach, marking a milestone in its expansion into one of Europe's largest telecommunications markets and a key international growth priority for the company. The new store, located in Offenbach, represents another step in Telekom Srbija's plan to establish a nationwide retail and distribution network in Germany. The opening of our 9th shop on March 26 marks an important step in building a nationwide presence as we invest from a position of strength with a clear long-term focus.". Germany plays a central role in Telekom Srbija's international expansion, both due to the size of its telecom sector and the presence of the largest Serbian diaspora in Europe.

context.content: # Amazon Deepens Europe Push With $18 Billion Germany Investment, AWS Expansion. **Amazon.com Inc.** (NASDAQ:AMZN) announced Tuesday that it plans to invest more than 16 billion euros (roughly $18 billion) in Germany in 2027, expanding its cloud, AI, logistics, and media operations as the company continues to build out its European footprint. The package includes 4.8 billion euros to expand the AWS Europe (Frankfurt) Region to meet demand for cloud and artificial intelligence services. The latest commitment adds to Amazon's existing presence in Germany, where the company said it has invested more than 100 billion euros since 2010, building more than 100 sites. It also follows Amazon's June announcement of a more than 10 billion euros investment to expand and modernize its European fulfillment network, including the deployment of next-generation robotics. This article Amazon Deepens Europe Push With $18 Billion Germany Investment, AWS Expansion originally appeared on Benzinga.com.

context.content: # Amazon plans €16bn investment across Germany in 2027. Amazon plans to invest more than €16bn ($18bn) in Germany in 2027, covering cloud, AI, satellite communications, logistics, and media production. The planned one-year spending adds to the more than €100bn the company reports investing in the country since 2010. Amazon chief global affairs and legal officer David Zapolsky said: "Germany is a hub of innovation and one of the most attractive investment opportunities in Europe. That is why we have invested more than €100bn here since 2010, and why we plan to invest an additional €16bn in 2027. Its streaming platform Prime Video plans to release more than 15 local productions in Germany by the end of 2027. Germany Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy Katherina Reiche added: "Amazon's investment is a clear vote of confidence in Germany as a location for the future. "Amazon plans €16bn investment across Germany in 2027" was originally created and published by Investment Monitor, a GlobalData owned brand.

# Deutsche Telekom invests in industrial AI data centre

Daniel Shepherd

Deutsche Telekom recent began preparations for another multi-million-euro investment in an industrial AI data centre it opened in Munich, Germany earlier this year.

The company approached Nvidia to boost capacity after being swamped by demand.

Nvidia’s B300 Blackwell Ultra Generation GPUs are being added to B200 systems already in play at the so-called AI Factory, doubling the number of such chips as Deutsche Telekom looks to take capacity to 20MW.

document.name: Deutsche Telekom invests in industrial AI data centre | TahawulTech.com

context.content:
The expansion follows strong demand for the facility, which launched in February 2026. Its first expansion phase was fully booked seven months later, and Telekom said it had begun planning further expansion phases in May. Siemens and Daimler Trucks are among the companies already using the infrastructure.

Other users named by the company include Currenta, Synopsis, Agile Robots, Wandelbots, PhysicsX, Noxtua, EDAG and Soofi. Applications range from industrial AI and robotics to simulations and language models. Telekom also cited Soofi, a German language model trained on its infrastructure. [...] In sum – what to know

Capacity increases – Deutsche Telekom will invest nearly another €250 million to expand its Munich AI factory to 20 megawatts, adding Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 systems.

Demand drives expansion – The facility’s first expansion phase was fully booked seven months after its February 2026 launch, prompting the company to add computing capacity.

Revenue ambitions grow – The investment supports DT’s broader AI strategy, which targets more than €1 billion in annual AI-related revenue outside the U.S. by 2030. [...] The company said the facility provides AI infrastructure designed to comply with European data protection, security and data-control requirements. It reported a power usage effectiveness (PUE) value of 1.2 and said waste heat generated by the facility will supply the entire Tucherpark district in the future.

Telekom is also exploring a possible further expansion of its operations in Bavaria with partners. Discussions are in an intensive phase, but the company stressed that implementation depends on financing, a sound financial framework and overall economic viability. No final investment decision has been made.

## Infrastructure expansion supports wider AI ambitions
